plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: Clouds of blush-white blossoms cover bare branches before the leaves appear. Each flower has five delicate petals and a faint almond scent. The trees line rivers, parks and castle moats, and they draw crowds for picnics under the petals.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to early April in central Japan. Early blooms can start in mid-March in warmer southern areas such as Kyushu and parts of Tokyo in early years.
plants.location: Japan, especially southern and central Honshu and Kyushu
plants.funFact: Nearly all Yoshino cherry trees are clones, grafted from a single original tree. This is why a whole city's trees tend to open within days of each other.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: Nodding, trumpet-shaped flowers glow in woodland clearings and meadows. A deep golden trumpet sits inside paler, swept-back petals. Drifts of them announce the end of winter across the countryside.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late February to late March, with a peak in March
plants.location: Western Europe, including England, Wales and northern France, in woods and damp meadows
plants.funFact: Daffodil bulbs contain alkaloids such as galantamine, which has been developed into a medicine for Alzheimer's disease. The same chemicals make the plant toxic to many grazing animals.

plants.name: Watsonia borbonica
plants.description: Tall spikes of tubular flowers rise above sword-shaped leaves. They are a favorite of sunbirds and other pollinators.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Cape, usually September to November. It is not in bloom on March 16.
plants.funFact: Many Cape bulbs flower after fires clear the vegetation.
